what: Lululemon sells athletic clothing: leggings, running and training wear, and increasingly menswear, through its own stores and website rather than through other retailers.
customers: People who exercise and people who dress as though they do, in North America, China and a growing number of other markets.
moat: A brand people pay a premium for and fabrics developed in-house, sold almost entirely through its own channels so it keeps the full retail margin rather than sharing it.
risks: North American sales growth has stalled as newer brands take share
The analyst average target is at the current price: nobody expects a quick recovery
Fashion risk: a few seasons of poor product design can cost years of brand momentum
opportunities: 8.7 times earnings and 5 times EBITDA, a valuation normally seen on failing retailers rather than one with a 14.2% net margin
$1.4B of free cash flow and $1.8B of cash against $1.8B of debt
China revenue is still growing quickly and is a fraction of the size of the American business
watch: North American comparable sales, which is what the valuation hangs on.
